title: Polynomial graph coinduction and its oriented Koszul dual
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in A$. Put $S=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $i:A\to S$ be the coefficient inclusion, and let $e:S\to A$ be evaluation $x_j\mapsto a_j$, so $ei=1_A$. Set $f_j=x_j-a_j$. In ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and derived coinduction $C_e:D(S)\to D(A)$ with precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. The augmentation of the ordered Koszul complex $K_S(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], placed in cohomological degrees $-n,\ldots,0$, is a bounded finite-free resolution of the evaluation module $A$. With the orientation fixed by the ordered variables, there is an isomorphism
$$C_e(S[0])\cong A[-n]\quad\text{in }D(A),$$
where the action on the right is the original $A$-module action. For every $T\in D(A)$ there is an isomorphism, natural in $T$,
$$C_e(S\otimes_{A,i}^{\mathbf L}T)\cong T[-n]\quad\text{in }D(A).$$
The tensor comparison here uses the $A$-action on $C_e(S)$ and $ei=1_A$. No Noetherianity, nonzero-ring assumption, boundedness or Tor hypothesis on $T$ is required; when $n=0$ these are the identity comparisons.

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq n$, evaluation of the first $j$ variables induces $S/(f_1,\ldots,f_j)\cong A[x_{j+1},\ldots,x_n]$. Indeed evaluation kills these generators, and the inverse sends coefficients and the remaining variables to their quotient classes; the two composites agree on all variables and coefficients, hence are identities by the polynomial universal property. In this quotient multiplication by $f_{j+1}=x_{j+1}-a_{j+1}$ is injective: writing a polynomial as $\sum_{k=0}^m b_k x_{j+1}^k$ over the other-variable ring, the coefficient of $x_{j+1}^{m+1}$ in its product is $b_m$; descending comparison forces every $b_k=0$. Thus the injectivity holds without any nonzero-ring assumption. For $j=n$ the quotient map is exactly $e$ and its coefficient section is $i$.

source.place: Polynomial evaluation calculation; auxiliary argument for duality.tex Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] with $R=M=S$ and the ordered list $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$: Step 1 verifies precisely its successive-multiplication injectivity hypothesis (no proper-ideal hypothesis is required). It gives zero positive homology of $K$. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], $K_0=S$ and the image of $d_1$ is $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$; hence the augmentation identifies $H_0(K)$ with $A$ by Step 1. The same definition gives finite free terms indexed by subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and zero terms above $n$. Reindexing $K_q$ in cohomological degree $-q$ gives the asserted bounded finite-free resolution of $A[0]$.

source.place: Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular); Tag 0622, Koszul complex and its degree-zero augmentation.

proof.text: Let $L^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(K,S[0])$, with the signed differential of [def-sc-koszul-dual-complex]. The complementary equivalences [lem-sc-koszul-complementary-equivalences] identify its cohomology in degree $j$ with $H_{n-j}(K)$ for $0\leq j\leq n$. Step 2 therefore gives $H^j(L)=0$ for $j\ne n$, including the zero terms outside this interval. Normalize the top isomorphism explicitly: a top cochain $\lambda$ maps to $e(\lambda(e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n))$. The differential formula gives image $(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ in $L^n=S$: each coordinate of a cochain in $L^{n-1}$ contributes $\pm f_j$, so the image contains and is contained in that ideal. Hence this map induces $H^n(L)\cong A$, sending the ordered top dual basis to $1$. It is $S$-linear with the target action through $e$. For $n=0$ it is the identity of $S=A$.

source.place: Tag 0BQZ (lemma-regular-immersion-ext), local complementary Koszul dual calculation with the top generator specified.

proof.text: Put $E=C_e(S[0])$. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], its scalar restriction is $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,S)$. The projective resolution of Step 2 and [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] compute this by $L^\bullet$. The comparison is natural under scalar postcomposition, so the cohomology isomorphisms are $S$-linear. Check the original $A$-action rather than lifting an isomorphism from $D(S)$: on the K-injective model $\operatorname{Hom}_S(A,J)$, for $b\in A$ and $c\in A$, one has $(b h)(c)=h(cb)=h(i(b)c)=i(b)h(c)$. Thus the coinduction action of $b$ equals the scalar action of $i(b)$. The $S$-linear top identification of Step 3 is therefore $A$-linear because $e(i(b))=b$. It follows that $H^j(E)=0$ for $j\ne n$ and $H^n(E)\cong A$ with its original action. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] in the abelian category of $A$-modules and use this oriented top identification: $E\cong A[-n]$ in $D(A)$.

Step 2 makes $A[0]$ perfect over $S$: its exhibited resolution is bounded finite free, hence bounded finite projective, as required by [lem-trf-perfect-algebra-coinduction-tensor]. Apply that theorem to $e:S\to A$ and $N=S\otimes_{A,i}^{\mathbf L}T\in D(S)$. It yields a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$
$$C_e(N)\cong N\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}E.$$
The theorem retains the precomposition $A$-action on $E$ and imposes no boundedness on $N$. Substitution of Step 4 gives $(S\otimes_{A,i}^{\mathbf L}T)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}A[-n]$. The remaining cancellation must use the coefficient inclusion $i$ and the evaluation $e$, not an unspecified $A$-action.

source.place: Tag 0BZE (lemma-RHom-is-tensor-special), specialized to the perfect evaluation quotient.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $T$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $S\otimes_A P$ is K-flat over $S$. The two derived tensors of Step 5 are thus computed by these representatives using [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. In the final tensor, the degree-$p$ element $(s\otimes v)\otimes b$ (with $v\in P^p$, $b\in A[-n]^n=A$) maps to $(-1)^{np}e(s)bv\in P[-n]^{p+n}$. Its inverse sends $v\in P[-n]^{p+n}$ to $(-1)^{np}(1\otimes v)\otimes1$. The tensor balancing identities use $e(i(a))=a$; they show these are inverse $A$-linear maps. They commute with differentials since the target differential is $(-1)^n d_P$, and the sign changes by $(-1)^n$ when $p$ increases by one. These formulas commute with all chain maps in $P$; canonical K-flat comparisons and functoriality in the cited tensor theorem therefore give a natural isomorphism with $T[-n]$ in $D(A)$. No boundedness or Tor condition has entered. When $n=0$, $e=i=1_A$, $K=S[0]$, and the top dual and tensor maps are the identity comparisons. If $A=0$ all the complexes above are zero and the same calculations apply.
